summary: Albert Graeter worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a missionary with the Basel Mission (circa 1859-1876) and taught English at the University of Basel (1870-1908).

Albert Grünwedel specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology. He earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Munich (1876-1883) under Ernst Kuhn, Ernst Trumpp, and others, later directing the Indische Abteilung at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1904-1921).
Albert Henry Allen was an Indologist who completed an A.B. at the University of California, Los Angeles by 1898 and an M.A. at Harvard University by 1900.

Albert Henry Arden worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Christ's College, Cambridge (circa 1858-1861) and later served as University Lecturer in Telugu and Tamil at the University of Cambridge (1882-1890).

Albert Henry Longhurst was a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied under John Marshall. He served as Superintendent of the Southern Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1910-1911).

Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, Berlin (Doktor), and Königsberg (Ph.D.) under scholars including Franz Bopp, and spent his career as a professor at the University of Greifswald (circa 1840-1883).
Albert Hofmann studied at the University of Zurich from circa 1925 to 1929. He subsequently held a post at Novartis from circa 1929 to 1971.

Albert Ippel was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg, Berlin, and Bonn (Ph.D.). He held posts at the University of Breslau (circa 1923-1940), Humboldt University of Berlin (1940), and the University of Hamburg (1947-1954).
Albert Johannes de Jong was an Indologist who completed his PhD at Utrecht University by 1917, supervised by Willem Caland.

Albert Joris van Windekens was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at KU Leuven under Albert Joseph Carnoy and Jean Filliozat. He became agrégé at Leuven in 1944 and directed the Centre international de dialectologie générale (circa 1968-1989).

Albert Joseph Carnoy was a linguist who earned his doctorate at KU Leuven (circa 1898-1902). He served as professor at KU Leuven (1902-1955) and held positions at Columbia University (1915-1918) and the University of California, Berkeley (1918-1919).

Albert Lutz worked in archaeology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer and pursued his career at Museum Rietberg, where he became curator for Chinese art in 1982 and director from 1998 to 2019.

Albert Schweitzer studied philosophy and religious studies at the University of Strasbourg (circa 1893-1913), the University of Tübingen (1899), and the German University of Prague under Wilhelm Deecke. He held a post at the University of Strasbourg (circa 1902-1912).

Albert Sechehaye was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure at the University of Geneva from circa 1891 to 1895. He later held a position at the University of Geneva from circa 1902 to 1946.

Albert Socin was a linguist who studied at the University of Basel (circa 1862-1866). He held posts at the University of Basel (circa 1870-1876), the University of Tübingen (circa 1876-1890), and the University of Leipzig (circa 1890-1899).

Albert Ten Eyck Olmstead was an archaeologist and historian who earned his degrees at Cornell University (circa 1898-1906). He held posts at the University of Missouri (1909-1917), the University of Chicago (1917-1929), and the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures (1929).

Albert Thumb studied linguistics and Indology at Freiburg (PhD, Habilitation), Heidelberg, and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and Rudolf Thurneysen. He held professorships at the universities of Freiburg (1895), Marburg (1901), and Strasbourg (1909).

Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He held posts at the University of Winnipeg (circa 1993-2013) and the University of Arizona beginning in 2013.

Albert von Le Coq was an archaeologist who studied at the Seminar for Oriental Languages (circa 1900-1902). He worked at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from circa 1902 to 1930, becoming Director of the Asian Department in 1914.
Alberto Todeschini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2010) and has served as a guest at Kyoto University.
